result:
The final answer is wrong. The proposed solution boxes the formula Skew(2^e) = (7·2^{2e-5}+4)/3, but its closing line gives "4.491212739452411". A skew-morphism count is an integer, so that decimal cannot be Skew(2^e) for any e. The two answers also contradict each other.

The boxed formula is also unsupported. The recurrence S_e = 4S_{e-1} − 4 is asserted with no derivation of the lifting enumeration, and the values 6, 20, 76, 300 are not checked against any known count. I recall that the published classification of skew morphisms of cyclic 2-groups (Kovács and Nedela) gives a different closed form, but I can't reproduce it reliably here, so I am not offering a replacement.

VERDICT: REJECT
CONFIDENCE: 4
